new_statements.quote: Tagom is a tonal language with two register tones H/L which play a major role in the marking of the tense system of the language, sometimes together with vowel alternation regarding the prefix vowel. [...] In the present tense, the root is marked with a low tone whereas the past is always marked with a high tone which extends to influence the tone of the attached affixes.
new_statements.citation: Aldawi, Maha A. 2022. Verbal number in Tagom – Rashad group. Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online 2022, article 3486 (27 pp.). Cologne. doi:10.18716/ojs/aaeo/2022_3486
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: (27 pp., text layer, doi 10.18716/ojs/aaeo/2022_3486, header on p. 1) -- extracted text p. 6, paragraph <5>: "Tagom is a tonal language with two register tones H/L which play a major role in the marking of the tense system of the language, sometimes together with vowel alternation regarding the prefix vowel. Though vowel alternation is common... still unknown. In the present tense, the root is marked with a low tone whereas the past is always marked with a high tone which extends to influence the tone of the attached affixes." Both halves of the reported quote are verbatim; the "[...]" elides the two vowel-alternation sentences. Whole-PDF grep: 0 hits for stress/accent/prominence/pit…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The Tegali cluster (described through its Tagom/Rashad dialect) is analysed as a two-tone register language (H/L) whose tone carries tense marking; no modern first-hand source says anything about word stress or its position. The only stress remarks are Stevenson's 1950s ones, transmitted second-hand: Tucker & Bryan 1966 (ch. 18b, from Stevenson): 'Stress would also seem to have some importance, but has not been fully investigated'; Stevenson 1956/57: 47, 49 and 1964: 86 (via Bashir 2025): stress 'plays a marked role' and 'stress and vowel change also play a part in tense-formation' -- modern authors (Bashir 2025, Aldawi 2022/2025) reinterpret this prominence as H/L tone. No source gives a stress-placement rule.
new_statements.exceptions: Aldawi 2025: 73 adds 'The existence of lexical tone still needs to be checked' (tone so far shown only to be grammatical); Tucker & Bryan 1966 (from Stevenson) report three tone levels but no tonal doublets.
new_statements.domain_note: Verb roots in citation/paradigm forms (mono- and disyllabic bound roots with person prefixes); Tagom dialect (Rashad town/hills, Glottolog rash1248), speakers interviewed in Khartoum 2018-2019. Not Tingal/Kajakja itself.
new_statements.identity_note: ting1253 is a Glottolog bookkeeping entry: ISO 639-3 CR 2010-011 (Persson & Hammarström, adopted 2011-05-18) merged Tingal [tie] into Tegali [ras] = tega1236 after a field check showed Tingal (= Kajakja/Kajaja, c. 520-2,100 speakers, Tegali Hills) is a dialect of the Tegali cluster; the only published mention of Tingal is hearsay in Stevenson 1956/57: 103. No source describes Tingal itself. The quoted statement describes Tagom (= Gom = Rashad-town dialect; Glottolog rash1248 'Rashad Town-Hills', a child of tega1236), a sister dialect within the classless Tegali cluster (Tagom, Tegali, Umale, Kajakja per Aldawi & Nashid 2018 after Blench 2013). Any catalog entry should be filed under tega1236 (Tegali), not under the retired code.

sources.quote: Tagom is a tonal language with two register tones H/L which play a major role in the marking of the tense system of the language, sometimes together with vowel alternation regarding the prefix vowel. [...] In the present tense, the root is marked with a low tone whereas the past is always marked with a high tone which extends to influence the tone of the attached affixes.
sources.note: Para <5>, p. 6: 'Tagom is a tonal language with two register tones H/L which play a major role in the marking of the tense system'; present = L on root, past = H spreading to affixes. Syllable structure 'moderately complex'. No mention of stress or accent anywhere (grep). Tagom = Gom = Rashad dialect of the Tegali cluster, sister dialect of Kajakja/Tingal.

sources.citation: Aldawi, Maha A. 2025. A first approach to Tagom verbal inflection and clausal negation strategies. In Idris, Junglas & Schneider-Blum (eds.), Nuba Mountain Language Studies: Contemporary Perspectives, 71-104. Cologne: USB Monographs (open access).
sources.note: p. 73 (sec. 2 Background): 'Tagom exhibits two register tones, a high tone and a low tone, which have a major role in its grammar marking... The existence of lexical tone still needs to be checked.' p. 79 quotes Stevenson 1956-57: 49 on Tegali/Tumale: 'Stress and vowel change also play a part in tense-formation'. No statement of stress placement.

sources.citation: Bashir, Abeer. 2025. Plural suffixes on Tagoi nouns. In Idris, Junglas & Schneider-Blum (eds.), Nuba Mountain Language Studies: Contemporary Perspectives, 41-70. Cologne: USB Monographs (open access).
sources.note: Sister cluster (Tagoi), but reports Stevenson on the whole Rashad group second-hand: p. 43 Stevenson (1956/57: 47) 'doubted whether tone exists or, "apart from stress, plays an important role" in Rashad languages'; p. 49 'Stevenson instead claims that stress plays a marked role and may be responsible for grammatical and lexical contrast in Tagoi (Stevenson 1956/1957: 47; 1964: 86)'; Bashir finds H/L tone instead and suggests Stevenson 'attributed it to stress'. No placement rule.

sources.note: 'probably all Kordofanian languages are tone languages (with generally two tone...)'; Rashadian = Tegali (eastern, classless) + Tagoi (western) clusters; no stress statement; cites Stevenson 1956/57 for Rashad data.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (A. Persson, H. Hammarström). 2010. Change Request 2010-011: merge [tie] Tingal into [ras] Tegali (adopted 2011-05-18). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Establishes identity: Tingal (Kajakja) is a dialect of Tegali, not of Tagoi; the only published mention is Stevenson 1956/57: 103 ('orally reported to be different from Tegali and Rashad'), copied by Tucker & Bryan 1956: 70.
